scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “A finitely generated counterexample to the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture” (preprints/A-finitely-generated-counterexample-to-the-Eilenberg-Ganea-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 249 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 bbc781ac6f173938), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a finitely generated residually finite group G such that cdZ G = 2, gd G = 3. One may take G to be the height kernel in the right-angled Artin group associated to a finite acyclic flag triangulation of the presentation complex ⟨x, y | x2 = y5 , x2 = (xy−1 )3 ⟩. (1.1) No two-dimensional classifying space for this G exists, regardless of the number of its cells.
